response: Routinely collected ambulance data about assaults can indeed contribute to the reduction in community violence. By using a hotspots approach to share data, it is possible to identify areas where assaults are most common without disclosing person-identifiable information. This approach has been shown to be effective, as at least half of the ambulance hotspots are unknown to the police. By sharing this data, law enforcement agencies can implement targeted interventions, such as anticipatory patrols or problem-oriented policing, to prevent and reduce community violence, particularly more severe assaults. Additionally, this data sharing can lead to improved efficiency of resource deployment, ultimately contributing to a reduction in community violence.
